summary.headline: Pearl Global FY26 consolidated revenue rose 11.5% to INR5,025 crore; adjusted EBITDA margin 9.3% (10.3% ex tariff and new-facility losses).
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR1,314 crore (+6.9% YoY) with adjusted EBITDA (ex-ESOP) of INR135 crore at a 10.3% margin, the highest quarterly margin to date. FY26 PAT rose 17% to INR270 crore, helped by cost restructuring, while India volumes fell sharply in Q4 as US tariffs shifted orders to other countries. Management guided to a 10% group EBITDA margin for FY27 and a 12-14% revenue CAGR, with FY28 capacity of 125-130 million pieces. The company also raised its dividend to a record INR14.50 per share for FY26.

segments.name: India (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 India revenue fell about 23% as the US tariff pushed orders out of India; management says Q4 India EBITDA ex-tariff was 9.6% versus 10.2% a year earlier. Target is high single-digit EBITDA for FY27 and double-digit in Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Bangladesh
segments.commentary: Strong export growth to the US, UK, EU, Spain and Canada; capex of about 6 million pieces due H1 CY2027, with two new units (washing and stitching) ready in H2 this year.

segments.name: Vietnam
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation rose to 80%+ from 63%; management is buying land for a greenfield project and considering in-house capacity over partner factories.

segments.name: Indonesia
segments.commentary: Utilisation rose to 47% from 39% last year; the company will buy an extra 10% of PT Pinnacle Apparels for $1.4 million, taking its stake to 99.92%.

segments.name: Guatemala
segments.commentary: Losses continuing; strategy reworked and management expects breakeven in FY27. The Other segment (Indonesia, Dubai, US, Guatemala) drove the Q4 spike, not Guatemala alone.

guidance_outlook: FY27 group adjusted EBITDA margin guided at about 10%, then 10-12% in subsequent years, with the 10% considered largely operational.
Revenue CAGR of 12-14% targeted at group level; management says the INR6,000 crore FY28 target (set in 2023) is achievable even at about 9% growth.
FY28 target: 125-130 million pieces of established capacity and about 100 million pieces shipped, to reach INR6,000 crore.
FY27 capex of INR200-250 crore being outlined across geographies; INR250 crore already committed for completion by H1 FY27.
Expected realisation gain from the removal of tariff costs, though hard to quantify as costing is reset each season; current realisation about INR635-640 per garment, with a goal of INR600+.
Guatemala expected to reach breakeven in FY27.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 101 million pieces per annum as of 31 March 2026, crossing 100 million ahead of an H1 FY27 target.
Bangladesh expansion adds about 6-7 million pieces in FY27; CWIP INR110 crore, expected to reach about INR150 crore after H1 FY27 capitalisation.
Vietnam land parcel identified; purchase consideration $2.5-3 million; greenfield plans to follow.
Management targets an additional 20-25 million pieces, combining capex and partner capacity, over the next two years; a laundry capex in Bangladesh will lift margins without adding top line.
Bihar plant is in ramp-up; the company adds capacity line by line, with partner factories used alongside in-house (target roughly 80-85% in-house).
demand_pricing: India order book is seeing good traction after the US tariff eased; EU and UK customers are interested in India under the FTAs, and some are seeking added capacity there.
US consumer demand has held up despite inflation; management says there is no sign yet of the weakness seen in 2022 at about $110 oil.
Raw material costs are typically passed through within 1-2 months of order booking, and fabric is bought once orders are placed.
Muji has crossed about $65 million in turnover and is in the top 6 clients; UNIQLO is not a current priority due to competitive overlap.
Discounts and burden-sharing to US clients during the tariff period weighed on India margins; part of the 10% US tariff is still being absorbed.
Design team grew from about 70-75 to just over 100 people.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India revenue fall about 23% in Q4 and what drove growth in the Other segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India orders shifted out under the high US tariff, with existing orders shipped by December-January. Growth in overseas business came from volume and value-added products in Bangladesh, Vietnam and Indonesia; the Other segment includes Indonesia, Dubai, US and Guatemala, not Guatemala alone.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 10% margin be sustained in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 10% is achievable for FY27, given the removal of reciprocal tariff costs and the Guatemala and Bihar ramp-up, with Q4 seasonally strongest.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR6,000 crore FY28 target consistent with INR630 realisation and 100 million pieces?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR6,000 crore target dates from 2023 and is expected to be exceeded; the company plans 12-14% group CAGR, with growth rotating across countries.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is needed beyond INR250 crore for 25-30 million pieces?
qa_highlights.answer: INR250 crore covers the committed program; FY27 capex could be INR200-250 crore, and the total may exceed that, combining in-house and partner capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tariff cost likely to be in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR36 crore tariff cost will fall significantly, possibly to INR5-8 crore, with some burden share continuing at about 10%.

risks_watch: US tariff regime: the Section 122 10% tariff runs only until July; refund claims after the Supreme Court ruling may be slow.
Energy-driven input cost inflation (cotton and polyester) and freight; manpower availability is a flagged risk.
Ramp-up risk for Bihar, Indonesia and Guatemala; Guatemala breakeven in FY27 is a target only.
Higher inventory days versus last year; management partly linked this to higher Q1 FY27 shipments.
Capex scope for FY27 (INR200-250 crore) and the Vietnam land deal are still under evaluation.
Timing of the India-EU and India-UK FTA implementation dates.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY27 margins and growth, with clear numbers on tariffs and capacity. Evasive on exact figures for realisation trajectory, Muji vendor share, and new-client counts, which management said are hard to predict.
key_quotes: And we are pretty confident at this stage to really maintain 10% EBITDA for the full year as we start FY '27.

So by 2028, what we had foreseen is that we should be having established capacity of anywhere between 125 million to 130 million, and we should be shipping around 100 million pieces to get to that target of INR6,000 crores that we spoke about.
So, 12% to 14% is something like we have been talking about as a CAGR that we have planned.
